abstract: Background. Efferocytosis after ischaemic stroke is usually inferred from bulk tissue transcripts and condensed into one score, which cannot separate a tissue containing more phagocytes from one whose phagocytes are more active; the gene sets behind such scores also mix clearance machinery with the inflammatory output that follows. Methods. We built a decoupled framework scoring apoptotic demand (DEMAND), clearance machinery (CAPACITY), immunogenic output (OUTCOME) and a brake. We assembled 38 datasets across brain, blood, PBMC and sorted parenchyma, admitted a score only where at least 75% of a program's genes were detected, and tested every claim against expression-matched nulls, lineage proxies and cell-level constraints. Because clearance consumes ATP, supply and demand were scored on one scale under one decision rule. Results. After adjustment for five leukocyte lineages the CAPACITY difference survived in one of three cohorts (+0.473, 95% CI +0.350 to +0.588), fell to +0.014 in the second and was unidentifiable in the third; the unadjusted differences (+0.613 and +0.374) exceeded expression- and detection-matched nulls, so the signal is real, but its compositional share differs by cohort. In matched PBMCs the point estimate was negative and not distinguishable from zero. In the only sorted human parenchyma series, non-microglial myeloid cells made up 0.371 of CD45-positive cells against 0.199 in controls, while every microglial layer fell below its expression-matched floor: it moves the composition boundary without testing capacity. In rodent brain it rose with injury: day 3 in microglia, day 7 in macrophages. Energy supply cleared both gates in eleven of eighteen contrasts and demand in eight, concentrated in entering cells (oxidative phosphorylation +1.512 in infiltrating macrophages at day 3). The two scores ranked samples almost identically ({rho} 0.59 to 0.95), and the one significant gap vanished under the same adjustment. Conclusions. Efferocytic transcripts are a measurement bounded by compartment, composition and time, not a flux assay or a biomarker. Energy supply rises with the work of clearance in the cells that carry it, and can rise in cells that do not engulf, but the two scores move closely enough that no transcript design can show one
